ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the horizontal axis is labeled f/MHz, and the power spectral density curve has a raised-cosine roll-off shape, centered near 10 MHz; the curve drops to zero at about 6 MHz and 14 MHz; there are also dashed vertical reference lines in the figure located at about 7 MHz and 13 MHz. Reasoning: The actual occupied bandwidth is given by the zero-point range, which is 14 - 6 = 8 MHz. The nominal Nyquist bandwidth without roll-off is given by the dashed reference range, which is 13 - 7 = 6 MHz. The raised-cosine roll-off factor alpha = (actual bandwidth - nominal bandwidth) / nominal bandwidth = (8 - 6) / 6 = 2/6 = 1/3.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: a raised-cosine-shaped PSD centered near 10 MHz, with zero crossings at 6 MHz and 14 MHz and dashed vertical reference lines at 7 MHz and 13 MHz. Compute actual occupied bandwidth as 14 - 6 = 8 MHz. Compute the nominal Nyquist bandwidth as 13 - 7 = 6 MHz. Apply alpha = (8 - 6) / 6 = 2/6 = 1/3.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the standard excess-bandwidth definition directly from the visually marked occupied band and nominal Nyquist band; no alternative accepted methods exist to distinguish from.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the PSD plot: the transmitted spectrum is nonzero from 6 MHz to 14 MHz, so the occupied bandwidth is 8 MHz. The dashed vertical markers are at 7 MHz and 13 MHz, indicating the nominal/flat Nyquist bandwidth of 6 MHz.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to identify the plotted spectrum as a raised cosine roll-off system and to know that the requested unknown is the roll-off factor.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a raised cosine roll-off system, the roll-off factor is the excess bandwidth divided by the minimum Nyquist bandwidth: alpha = (B_actual - B_Nyquist) / B_Nyquist.
